lines.text: Antarctica's ice melts, all of it. Which countries vanish from the map first?
From space, Antarctica is a whole white continent at the bottom of the world, buried under ice so thick it hides whole mountain ranges.
Melt it, and all that water runs into the one ocean that touches every coast on Earth. So where does it hit first?
Start in Europe. The Netherlands is low, flat land, and the North Sea pours in until most of it is gone, Amsterdam and Rotterdam included.
Fly east to Bangladesh, a country of river mouths. Most of it slips under the Bay of Bengal, and the capital, Dhaka, goes with it.
Across the Atlantic, the sea closes in on Florida's long peninsula, and most of the state is under water too.
But those three keep their high ground. So which countries lose everything?
Out in the Indian Ocean lie the Maldives, hundreds of coral islands, none much higher than a house. Every one goes under. A whole country, gone.
Then the Pacific: Tuvalu and the Marshall Islands, whole nations built on low rings of coral, wiped off the map.
All because the sea would stand about 58 m higher than it does today, and their highest ground is nowhere near that.
Netherlands or Florida: which new coastline surprised you more? Tell me below, before Antarctica's ice melts, all of it.
